name: arc-enclosed-region-fill
description: Use when an ARC grid has line-drawn shapes enclosing blank regions. Fill enclosed interiors with color 4 while preserving outlines and exterior.
---

# Fill enclosed ARC regions

## Rule
When a grid shows a uniform background crossed by a non-background line pattern that forms one or more closed boundaries, recolor the cells strictly inside the closed boundary/boundaries to **4**. Preserve all existing non-background outline cells and all exterior/background cells. The outline and background colors can vary; do not assume a fixed palette for them.

Evidence from the solved instance: a demo with background 7 and outline 9 changed only the interior cells of closed rectangular regions to 4. The test had background 5 and outline 8; filling the enclosed interior with 4 while preserving all other cells solved it.

## Procedure
1. Identify the dominant background color and the non-background line/outline color(s).
2. Locate regions enclosed on all sides by the outline. Use connectivity/topology, not just a bounding box: cells are interior only if separated from the exterior by the outline.
3. Change only those interior background cells to color 4.
4. Keep the grid dimensions, background, all outline cells, and any un-enclosed areas unchanged.
5. Validate that each recolored area is actually enclosed and that no outline/exterior cells changed.

## Caution
The demonstration and test establish the fill color as 4 for this task family, even though the background and outline colors differ. Do not recolor the whole shape or the background. If a future example contradicts this, prioritize the new evidence.",
